title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler is re-deriving Lagrange's 1766–69 integration of the separated equation dx/√X = dy/√Y, where X = A+Bx+Cx²+Dx³+Ex⁴ and Y is the same quartic in y. The aim is to show that Lagrange's algebraic integral is equivalent to Euler's own canonical symmetric biquadratic relation between x and y.

On the previous page Lagrange's trick gives (√X+√Y)/(x−y) = √(Δ + D(x+y) + E(x+y)²), with Δ an arbitrary constant. Squaring this, and removing (D(x+y)+E(x+y)²)(x−y)² from X+Y, Euler proceeds as follows.

(1) Top of this page. The integral becomes [2A + B(x+y) + C(x²+y²) + Dxy(x+y) + 2Ex²y² + 2√(XY)]/(x−y)² = Δ.

(2) §40. He subtracts C from both sides, using C(x²+y²) − C(x−y)² = 2Cxy, and sets Γ = Δ − C. This gives [V + 2√(XY)]/(x−y)² = Γ, where V = 2A + B(x+y) + 2Cxy + Dxy(x+y) + 2Ex²y². Hence 2√(XY) = Γ(x−y)² − V. Squaring gives 4XY − V² = Γ²(x−y)⁴ − 2ΓV(x−y)².

(3) §41. He expands 4XY completely as a symmetric polynomial. He then begins expanding V², which is finished on the next page.

Purpose of the next pages: show that 4XY − V² has the factor (x−y)², divide it out, and obtain a symmetric quadratic-in-each-variable relation. That relation is Euler's 'canonical equation', so Lagrange's integral and Euler's addition-theorem integral are identified.
errors: No errors found. I checked: the reduction X+Y − (D(x+y)+E(x+y)²)(x−y)² = 2A+B(x+y)+C(x²+y²)+Dxy(x+y)+2Ex²y²; the shift by C giving 2Cxy; the squaring step; and all 15 terms of 4XY (e.g. 4BDxy(x²+y²), 4BExy(x³+y³), 4CEx²y²(x²+y²)). The partial expansion of V² (4AA, 4AB(x+y), 8ACxy, 4ADxy(x+y), 8AEx²y², B²(x+y)², …) also matches the correct square of V.

ideas.what: Turning Lagrange's integral (√X+√Y)/(x−y) = √(Δ+D(x+y)+E(x+y)²) into a rational form. This is done by isolating 2√(XY) with the constant shift Γ = Δ − C and then squaring.
ideas.modern_name: Rationalization of the addition-theorem integral for elliptic differentials; symmetric biquadratic (Euler) relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (method, Misc. Taurinensia c. 1766–69); Euler (canonical biquadratic, 1750s–60s)
ideas.where_published: E506 itself. Euler's canonical-equation treatment appears in his earlier papers on the elliptic addition theorem (e.g. E251/E252, E261) and in the Institutiones calculi integralis.

ideas.what: Full term-by-term expansion of 4XY for two general quartics, and of V², in preparation for factoring out (x−y)².

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine, correct algebra in a well-known published commentary on Lagrange's method. Euler is reconciling Lagrange's integral with his own canonical biquadratic, which historians of elliptic integrals already treat. Nothing new here.
transcription_corrections: Transcription is essentially faithful. In the first displayed equation the image writes 2E x²y² and C(x²+y²) as transcribed.
The page ends mid-term with '+4B', continued on the next page as '+4BCxy(x+y)'.
